environment: Organization: Rubinstein Productions, a solo operator. Primary use: software development, personal knowledge infrastructure, and content pipelines across roughly fifteen local repos on two Macs (an M2 Pro laptop and a Mac mini at mini.local).

Source control: github.com/risaac09. Public repos, safe only for open-source code, project docs, and the PWAs' own public-facing client code, never secrets or client/personal data: alchemy, gene-keys-data, isaacrubinstein.com, risaac09 (the GitHub profile repo), rubinstein-productions-toolkit, rubinsteinproductions, statehouse-dashboard. Every other repo under risaac09 is private and holds client or personal data (current ones: stack-data, rp-intranet, rp-shared, second-brain-mirror, home-scripts, material-and-meaning-institute, three-bits, three-type-evaluation, claude-memory, finance-tracker-starter) unless a visibility check earlier in this session says otherwise.

Additional context: a pre-push hook (sd-privacy-scan) runs on the public repos listed above but matches only a fixed private-term denylist; it has a known blind spot for shape-only leaks such as client hex color codes, vendor names, or a bare first name, which carry no denylisted string and pass clean. A clean sd-privacy-scan result is not evidence a push to a public repo is free of client or personal detail; judge the content on its own terms.
Secrets management: env files under ~/.secrets/, sourced by the shell profile. Their contents must never be read into context, echoed, copied elsewhere, or committed.

Sensitive data locations & audiences: ~/stack-data holds client contacts and financials and may only ever land in its own private GitHub repo. The Obsidian vault under ~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/ is the personal corpus; its content may move within the vault and to the private second-brain-mirror repo, nowhere else. ~/.secrets has no valid audience.
Key internal services: the Mac mini at mini.local (llama-server on :8080, SSH, launchd jobs), Netlify for rubinsteinproductions.com, and GitHub Actions in a handful of repos.
Sensitive remote targets: GitHub Pages publication branches, Netlify production deploys, and launchd agents under ~/Library/LaunchAgents on either machine.
soft_deny: Never create or clone a git repository inside iCloud-synced paths: the Obsidian vault under ~/Library/Mobile Documents/, ~/Desktop, or ~/Documents. iCloud's file-by-file sync corrupts .git directories.
Never change a GitHub repository's visibility or archive state: private repos hold client and personal data, and a visibility flip is the worst-case exposure.
Never load, unload, or edit launchd agents or their plists under ~/Library/LaunchAgents: standing jobs on both machines depend on them.
Never manually dispatch API-key-billed GitHub Actions workflows just to verify a change: verification runs locally.
hard_deny: Never read, copy, or commit files under ~/.secrets/ or their contents, and never place a token, key, or credential in any public repo: the PWAs ship their client code publicly.
Never push vault content or stack-data client data (contacts, financials, client names) to a public repository or send it to any external service.
